newsitem.title: INDIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - May 22.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - May 22.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Indian business and political stories in leading newspapers prepared for REUTERS by Business News and Information Services Pvt Ltd, New Delhi Tel:3324842, 3351006, 3761233 Fax:+91-11-3351006 Internet: biznis@giasbm01.vsnl.net.in
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
TOP STORIES
The Times Of India
BATTLE LINES DRAWN IN WOMEN'S QUOTA BILL

The debate on the controversial women's reservation Bill threatened to get sharper. The Bill, seeking 33 percent reservation for women in Parliament and legislatures, has unsettled all political parties. It led to a divide not just within the ruling United Front (UF) constituents but also within the opposition Bharatiya Janata Party. The Left criticised the UF for its handling of the Bill in Parliament, saying the demand for reservation for other backward class (low caste) women was a ploy to stall the Bill. The Left parties, ranged against other UF constituents, were set to discuss the Bill at the UF steering committee meeting on May 25, which promises to be a stormy affair.
The Hindustan Times
CONGRESS CHIEF PLEDGES LOYALTY TO SONIA GANDHI

Congress president Sitaram Kesri pledged loyalty to Sonia Gandhi, widow of former prime minister Rajiv Gandhi, and hailed her leadership as the party's organisational elections in progress threatened to turn into a bitter tug of war among the party's bigwigs. Kesri's assertion of loyalty to the Gandhi family was seen as an attempt to remove the impression that he was reluctant to back her. Meanwhile, a function organised by the Congress youth wing to pay homage to Rajiv Gandhi on his sixth death anniversary, turned into a fiasco with Kesri, who was the chief guest, being prevented from delivering his speech.
The Economic Times
CRB AFFAIR HITS NON-BANKING FINANCIAL FIRM SCRIPS

Scrips of almost all non-banking finance companies (NBFCs) are bearing the brunt of the investigation into CRB Capital Markets by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) and federal police. The shares of many finance companies fell below their 52-week lows as investors made hasty exits from finance company stocks. Analysts said investors' behavioral patterns were shaped by fears that other finance companies with large liabilities to the public may also face a run on their deposits following the CRB Caps episode.
BAT HIKES STAKE IN ITC

Britain's BAT Industries had acquired proxies from the Rothmans group, which holds about 1.5 percent in ITC Limited. With this, BAT's effective control in ITC has increased to 33 percent. BAT is now close to equalling a 34 percent controlling stake held by Indian financial institutions. Under the new takeover code, BAT has informed the stock exchanges that its effective control in ITC has increased to 33 percent.
RHONE-POULENC VETS ENTRY INTO TYRE YARN

French chemicals giant, Rhone-Poulenc, is exploring the possibility of entering the industrial yarn and truck tyre business in India. Senior company officials said the Indian market, especially the polyamide knitting yarns and polyester sectors, is not large enough to warrant investment in Nylon 6,6 by itself. However, a venture to make yarn for truck tyres appears to be a viable proposition, they added. The group is scouting for joint venture partners and would take a minority stake in any forthcoming partnership, they added.
Financial Express
US BRIDGESTONE TO HIKE STAKE IN INDIA VENTURE

Tyre giant Bridgestone would hike its stake in Bridgestone ACC India from 51 percent to 64 percent. Another 10 percent equity is being picked up by Mitsui of Japan. This would result in a sharp reduction in ACC's equity stake from 49 percent to 26 percent. The proposal to make a drastic change in the equity structure of the joint venture has been cleared by the Foreign Investment Promotion Board.
ITC TO ADOPT CORPORATE GOVERNANCE CODE

The ITC board had decided to adopt a code of corporate governance, making it the first professionally managed company to do so. A management committee comprising executive directors and heads of key divisions for its implementation would be set up soon. The decision is aimed at having transparency in the functioning of the company. A financial institution nominee on the company's board was asked to prepare a draft report which was accepted at a board meeting.
